# LLM Lab: implementing and testing language-model foundations

::: {.project-meta}
**Type:** personal technical learning and experimentation project  
**Focus:** Python · NumPy · transformer inference · numerical testing · reproducible experiments  
**Status:** implementation and educational experiments; not a trained or production model
:::

## Why this project

LLM Lab is a code-first exploration of the foundations of large language models. The aim is to make key mechanisms inspectable: implement them, test their behaviour, compare numerical results with a reference implementation, and explain the concepts through a bilingual Quarto learning path.

The project is both a learning resource and a public engineering artifact. Its claims are deliberately limited to what the code, tests, and published experiments demonstrate.

## Implementation

The repository contains a NumPy decoder-only GPT inference path, including attention, causal masking, autoregressive generation, and decoding policies.

- [GPT model implementation](https://github.com/JM-Brun/llm-lab/blob/main/src/llm_lab/foundations/gpt.py)
- [Attention implementation](https://github.com/JM-Brun/llm-lab/blob/main/src/llm_lab/foundations/attention.py)
- [Generation and decoding](https://github.com/JM-Brun/llm-lab/blob/main/src/llm_lab/foundations/generate.py)

This implementation makes the computation explicit and testable. It is an inference reference: it does not train model parameters, and the default configuration uses random initialization.

## Numerical verification

The test suite checks model and generation behaviour, including tensor shapes, input validation, deterministic decoding, causal prefix invariance, and numerical properties.

A dedicated reference-parity test maps the same randomly initialized parameters into the NumPy implementation and Hugging Face GPT-2, then compares logits and hidden states with dtype-appropriate tolerances.

- [Model tests](https://github.com/JM-Brun/llm-lab/blob/main/tests/unit/test_gpt.py)
- [Generation tests](https://github.com/JM-Brun/llm-lab/blob/main/tests/unit/test_generate.py)
- [GPT-2 reference-parity tests](https://github.com/JM-Brun/llm-lab/blob/main/tests/unit/test_gpt2_reference_parity.py)

This is evidence of implementation-level numerical agreement under the tested setup. It is not a comparison against a pretrained checkpoint and does not establish language quality.

## A bounded decoding experiment

The project includes a small, reproducible experiment showing how temperature and top-k filtering alter a synthetic four-logit distribution. The report records entropy and retained probability mass and explains what the experiment can and cannot establish.

- [Decoding-distribution experiment](https://github.com/JM-Brun/llm-lab/blob/main/reports/decoding-distribution.md)
- [Experiment protocol](https://github.com/JM-Brun/llm-lab/blob/main/docs/experiment-protocol.md)

The example is an explanatory numerical experiment, not a benchmark of model performance or generated text quality.

## Engineering and communication

The repository combines a structured Python package, automated tests, static analysis and typing configuration, experiment protocols, machine-readable results, and a bilingual Quarto learning site. The learning path connects conceptual explanations to code and small experiments.

- [Project repository](https://github.com/JM-Brun/llm-lab)
- [Published learning site](https://jm-brun.github.io/llm-lab/)
- [Project status and scope](https://github.com/JM-Brun/llm-lab/blob/main/docs/project-status.md)

## What this demonstrates

The public artifacts provide inspectable evidence of:

- implementing transformer inference components in Python and NumPy;
- reasoning about tensor operations, causal attention, and autoregressive decoding;
- writing tests for numerical and behavioural invariants;
- comparing an implementation with a reference under controlled parameter mapping;
- designing bounded experiments and documenting their limitations;
- communicating technical concepts through structured, bilingual documentation.

## Limitations

The current project should not be interpreted as evidence of a completed training pipeline, fine-tuning workflow, pretrained-checkpoint evaluation, production deployment, or model-quality benchmark. The reference-parity test uses shared random parameters; the decoding report uses a synthetic four-logit vector. These boundaries are part of the result, not footnotes to hide.

The project is an evolving learning and engineering laboratory. Its value here is the inspectable implementation, verification approach, and clarity about what remains unimplemented.
